material_systems.name: Interior Adhesion Primer
material_systems.description: Water-based adhesion promoter for previously painted interior trim. Bonds to glossy, chalky, or oil-based existing coatings without full mechanical sanding. Primary RP primer for sound-to-peeling conditions where adhesion enhancement is needed. Trim is the highest-risk surface for oil-based existing paint — coating ID test in assessment phase is critical.

products.notes: Water-based for low VOC and easy cleanup. Bonds to glossy surfaces without full mechanical sanding. For SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: use only when adhesion test is marginal or existing sheen is semi-gloss+. For SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime all scraped areas, full prime if bare >30%. For SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime after complete scrape. Trim historically received oil-based paint — adhesion primer is especially critical when solvent test confirms alkyd base.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: conditional — skip if adhesion test passes on low-sheen surfaces; apply if marginal adhesion or high-sheen existing finish or oil-based base identified
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped areas (<30% bare) or full prime (>=30% bare)
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime — extensive bare area after complete scrape

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Interior Stain-Blocking Primer (Shellac-Based)
material_systems.description: Shellac-based stain blocker for smoke-damaged trim. Full-surface application required — smoke contamination is pervasive even when not visually apparent on trim surfaces. Latex and acrylic primers have ZERO stain blocking capability (RC-002). Trim in smoke-damaged homes may have concentrated nicotine deposits in profile crevices.

products.notes: Shellac is the ONLY product that reliably seals nicotine/smoke residue. Full surface application required. Strong odor — requires ventilation. Fast dry (~45 min recoat). NOT water-cleanup — requires denatured alcohol for tool cleaning. Trim profiles may trap concentrated smoke deposits in crevices — ensure full coverage of profile details.

material_systems.cleanup: Denatured alcohol. Standard water cleanup does NOT work for shellac. CON_DENATURED_ALCOHOL required.

material_systems.name: Interior Mildew-Resistant Primer
material_systems.description: Mildew-resistant primer with antimicrobial additives for moisture-damaged trim. Applied after biocide treatment and full drying. Common on bathroom and kitchen trim where moisture exposure causes mildew growth at trim-to-wall joints and behind trim profiles. Gate condition: moisture SOURCE must be resolved before painting.

products.notes: Apply only after biocide treatment and full drying (24+ hrs). Contains antimicrobial additives preventing spore regrowth under paint film. Gate condition: active moisture source MUST be resolved by other trades. Bathroom/kitchen trim is the most common application — moisture enters at trim-to-wall joints.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE: full surface prime on all affected trim — mildew spores may be present beyond visible damage area

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: 100% acrylic enamel for standard residential trim repaint at QT3. Fast dry/recoat, non-yellowing, water cleanup. Standard production grade for trim RP. Identical product selection to NC trim finish.

example_products: Sherwin-Williams ProClassic Waterborne Interior Acrylic Enamel
Benjamin Moore Regal Select Interior Semi-Gloss
products.notes: Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Standard production grade. Same product as NC trim finish at QT3.

material_systems.notes: Standard production system for QT3 trim RP. Satin is the only sheen available at QT3 per sheen/QT gate. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion on product selection (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Urethane-modified alkyd / waterbased alkyd for premium residential trim repaint at QT4. Superior flow and leveling, harder cured film. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Do not overwork. Sands easily between coats.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Advance Waterborne Interior Alkyd
Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane
products.notes: Superior flow and leveling. Harder cured film. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Do not overwork. Sands easily between coats. Same product as NC trim finish at QT4.

material_systems.notes: Premium residential standard for QT4 trim RP. Semi-gloss is typical at this tier. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Premium Urethane Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Premium acrylic-urethane enamel for superior trim repaint at QT5. Maximum durability, excellent leveling, hardest film. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Emerald Urethane is an acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT a waterborne alkyd (RC-006).

products.coat_notes: QT5 brush typically requires 3 coats per FFD 15.10.3. QT5 spray: 2 coats standard.
products.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Hardest film. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Emerald Urethane is an acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT a waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Sands easily between coats. Same product as NC trim finish at QT5.

material_systems.notes: Premium/custom home standard for QT5 trim RP. Gloss available only at this tier. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

coverage_profiles.notes: Adhesion primer on previously painted trim. Low-porosity substrate = higher coverage than bare-wood primer. Profile complexity affects surface area per LF. Per PDCA standard: 1 LF trim = 1 SF. Standard profile (ogee/cove) is baseline.
assumptions: Previously painted substrate — lower absorption than bare wood
Profile complexity modifiers: simple=+11%, complex=-11%, ornate=-17% from standard baseline

coverage_profiles.notes: Shellac-based stain blocker has lower coverage than latex adhesion primer due to higher solids content and thinner application film. Profile crevices on trim trap smoke residue, requiring thorough coverage of all profile surfaces.
assumptions: Full surface application on smoke-damaged trim
Shellac products have higher solids, lower spread rate than latex
Profile crevices require additional material to fully seal

coverage_profiles.notes: Mildew-resistant primer coverage similar to adhesion primer — latex-based formula with standard spread rate. Slightly lower than adhesion primer due to thicker recommended film build for antimicrobial effectiveness.
assumptions: Full surface application on moisture-damaged trim
Latex formula — similar coverage to adhesion primer
Slightly thicker film build recommended for antimicrobial effectiveness

coverage_profiles.notes: Finish coat coverage on primed trim surface. Identical to NC trim finish coverage (COV_TRIM_FINISH) because substrate condition after prime is equivalent. Standard profile (ogee/cove) is baseline at 400 LF/gal. Per PDCA standard: 1 LF trim = 1 SF. Coat count: QT3-QT4=2 coats, QT5 brush=3 coats per FFD 15.10.3.
assumptions: Primed smooth trim surface — equivalent to NC trim after prime
Two-coat system standard; third coat at QT5 brush has same per-coat coverage

consumables.name: RP Assessment Kit (adhesion test + coating ID)
consumables.specification: Cross-hatch cutter, pressure-sensitive tape (ASTM D3359), mineral spirits, white rags for coating identification solvent test
consumables.notes: RP-specific assessment supplies. One kit per project. Includes ASTM D3359 cross-hatch adhesion test materials and solvent test supplies for latex vs oil-based coating identification. Trim is HIGH RISK for oil-based existing paint — coating ID is critical. Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: Liquid Sander / Deglosser
consumables.specification: Liquid sander/deglosser for chemical degloss of existing paint, Krud Kutter Gloss-Off or equivalent
consumables.notes: RP-specific: chemical degloss for existing paint. Dulls existing sheen to promote adhesion without full mechanical sanding. Alternative to mechanical degloss (sanding). Especially useful on profiled trim where mechanical sanding cannot reach all crevices. Not used in NC trim specs.

consumables.name: Contour Scraper for Profile Trim
consumables.specification: Contour scraper set with interchangeable profiles for molding/trim scraping
consumables.notes: RP-specific: contour scrapers for profiled trim prep on failing/peeling paint. Conforms to profile shapes (ogee, cove, crown) for effective scraping without damaging substrate. Distinct from standard flat putty knife. Reusable tool — one set per crew.

consumables.name: Contour Sanding Sponge
consumables.specification: Flexible sanding sponge, medium/fine grit (150-220), angled edges for profile conformance
consumables.notes: Flexible sanding sponge for profiled trim prep and interstage. Conforms to crown, ogee, and complex profiles where rigid blocks cannot reach. For RP degloss on profiles and interstage sanding between coats on profiled surfaces. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine: flexible sponges for profile-following only, NOT for defect leveling (use rigid block for flat surfaces).

consumables.name: Sandpaper 120-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 120 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: Aggressive grit for feathering scrape edges on failing/peeling trim. Creates smooth transition from scraped to sound paint. Non-negotiable at all tiers — feathering must be thorough on trim (viewed at close range).

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 150 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: General prep grit for degloss scuff sanding and mechanical surface preparation on sound paint. All tiers.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 220 grit, 9x11 inch

grit_by_tier.QT3: 220 — spot sand nibs and rough spots only

consumables.notes: Interstage sanding between finish coats. Spot sand at QT3, full surface at QT4. Also used for light sand of primer before finish. Rigid sanding block mandatory for defect removal per FFD 15.4.1.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 320 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: QT5 interstage sanding between finish coats. 220-320 grit range at QT5. Uniform scratch pattern required. Rigid sanding block mandatory per FFD 15.4.1.

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.specification: Rigid sanding block, fine grit range (150-220)
consumables.notes: Rigid blocks remove defects — mandatory per FFD 15.4.1 for between-coat sanding on flat trim surfaces. Flexible sponges are NOT acceptable for defect leveling. Use CON_SANDING_SPONGE_CONTOUR for profiled areas only. One block per crew, reusable across coats.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5 inch)
consumables.specification: 2-2.5 inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle (nylon/polyester blend)
consumables.notes: Primary brush application tool for trim finish and primer. One per painter per material type (primer brush + finish brush). Also used for touch-up with spray method. Quality brush essential for smooth finish — do not skimp at higher QTs. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: 1 brush per material type.

consumables.name: Brush for shellac (dedicated)
consumables.specification: 2-inch angled sash brush, dedicated for shellac use, natural or synthetic bristle
consumables.notes: Dedicated brush for shellac stain-blocking primer (BIN). Shellac requires alcohol cleanup — keep separate from latex brushes. Conditional on smoke damage substrate state.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 310-411 (fine finish)
consumables.specification: Airless spray tip, 310-411 range (6-8 inch fan, 0.010-0.011 orifice) for fine-finish trim
consumables.notes: Fine-finish spray tips for trim (311-413 range). Tight fan pattern for trim width. Fine atomization for smooth finish. Distinct from wall tips (517-619). Tip life extends across many LF of trim.

consumables.name: Spray gun filter
consumables.specification: In-line filter for airless spray gun
consumables.notes: Replace when clogged or every ~50 gallons. One per spray setup.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.specification: Resin-impregnated cheesecloth for dust removal
consumables.notes: Wipe trim immediately before each coat application to remove sanding dust. Essential for quality finish per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 15.12. One tack cloth covers ~200 LF of trim. Use before every coat for dust-free surface.

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.specification: Paintable acrylic latex caulk, white, 10.1 oz tube
consumables.notes: For caulk assess/replace on RP trim joints. RP rate: ~200-300 LF per tube because only 15-30% of joints typically need replacement (per RF-008). NC rate was 72 LF/tube for full caulk of all joints. RP yield is higher because it is selective replacement. Clean old caulk residue before re-caulking. Allow cure time before coating.

consumables.name: Caulk gun
consumables.specification: Standard caulk gun, ratchet-type
consumables.notes: Reusable tool for caulk application. One per crew.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackling compound
consumables.specification: Lightweight spackling compound, tub or squeeze tube
consumables.notes: For patching scrape edges, filling gouges, and repairing defects revealed after degloss/scrape on RP trim. GOOD condition typically has no fill work. FAIR/POOR condition: fill scraped transition areas, surface defects, and small patches. Less usage than NC (no fastener fill) but more than wall RP (trim defects are close-range visible).

consumables.name: Flexible putty knife
consumables.specification: Flexible putty knife, 1.5-inch or 2-inch
consumables.notes: For applying lightweight spackle to defects and scrape edges. Flexible blade for flush fill on trim profiles. One per crew, reusable.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth runner
consumables.specification: Canvas drop cloth, 4x12 ft or 4x15 ft runner
consumables.notes: Perimeter floor protection during trim work. Runner-style drops along trim work area for drip catching. 1-2 per painter, reusable. RP always has finished floors — floor protection is mandatory. Required at all tiers and methods.

consumables.name: Blue painter's tape 1.5-inch
consumables.specification: Blue painter's tape, 1.5-inch width, 180 LF per roll (60 yards)
consumables.notes: For wall masking at trim edge. Required for spray method (tape line to attach masking paper). Required for brush method in RP because walls are always SS_PAINTED_* (finished). Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: 180 LF (60 yards) per roll regardless of width.

consumables.name: Masking paper 12-inch
consumables.specification: Masking paper, 12-inch width, 180 LF per roll (60 yards)
consumables.notes: For wall masking at trim edge during spray application. 12-inch width covers wall adjacent to trim. Attached with blue tape. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: 180 LF (60 yards) per roll. Spray method only — brush method uses tape line only, no paper needed.

consumables.name: Delicate surface tape (yellow)
consumables.specification: Delicate surface tape, 1.5-inch width, low tack, 180 LF per roll (60 yards)
consumables.notes: Use when walls are freshly painted or have delicate finish. Low tack prevents paint pull on removal. Substitute for blue tape when wall finish integrity is a concern. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: 180 LF per roll.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 4 mil
consumables.specification: 4 mil plastic sheeting for extended floor/furniture protection during spray
consumables.notes: Extended floor coverage for spray application in occupied homes. Heavier weight (4 mil) prevents tear during work and foot traffic. Covers broader floor area beyond canvas runner perimeter when spraying.

consumables.name: Outlet/switch cover
consumables.specification: Plastic fixture covers or masking film squares
consumables.notes: Covers for electrical outlets and switches near spray zone. Spray method only. Quantity driven by PS_PROTECT_EA.ASSET.FIXTURES.

consumables.name: Denatured alcohol
consumables.specification: Denatured alcohol for shellac cleanup
consumables.notes: For cleaning shellac stain-blocking primer from brushes and equipment. Required only when SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT is used (smoke damage). Standard water cleanup does NOT work for shellac.

floor_perimeter.description: Runner-style drop cloths along trim work area perimeter for drip containment
floor_perimeter.condition: always — RP always has finished floors
floor_perimeter.notes: Perimeter drops along baseboard and trim run areas. Mandatory at all tiers and methods.

wall_adjacent.description: Wall masking at trim-to-wall edge to protect finished walls
wall_adjacent.condition: always in RP — walls are always finished

method_scaling.brush: Tape line only (CON_MASKING_TAPE_BLUE) — no paper needed for brush
method_scaling.spray: Tape + paper masking (CON_MASKING_TAPE_BLUE + CON_MASKING_PAPER) — full overspray protection

wall_adjacent.notes: Wall masking is the critical adjacency protection for trim RP. In RP context, walls are ALWAYS finished (SS_PAINTED_*). Brush method: tape at wall-trim junction only. Spray method: tape + 12-inch masking paper.

fixture_covers.notes: Tape over nearby outlets and switches when spraying trim. Spray method only.

furniture_room.description: Move furniture and contents away from trim work zones in occupied homes
furniture_room.notes: RP-specific zone for occupied home context. Trim RP furniture protection is lighter than wall RP — trim work has a smaller spatter/overspray zone. Baseboard: clear floor-level items. Crown: clear shelf/mantel items near ceiling. Spray method requires broader furniture coverage.

compatibility_rules.description: All three finish systems are compatible with SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT
compatibility_rules.notes: Water-based adhesion primer accepts all fine-finish topcoats. Light sand primer before finish coat.

compatibility_rules.description: All three finish systems are compatible with SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT
compatibility_rules.notes: Shellac stain blocker is universally compatible as a base for any topcoat system. Light sand before finish coat.

compatibility_rules.description: All three finish systems are compatible with SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT
compatibility_rules.notes: Mildew-resistant primer accepts all fine-finish topcoats. Light sand primer before finish coat.

compatibility_rules.description: Latex finish over oil-based existing coating requires adhesion primer
compatibility_rules.notes: MANDATORY: When coating ID test confirms oil/alkyd existing paint, SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT is required before any latex finish. Trim is the highest-risk surface for this failure mode (FM-001).

risk_notes.risk: Applying latex finish directly over unknown oil/alkyd base without adhesion primer. Trim is the highest-risk surface for this failure mode.
risk_notes.mitigation: Coating identification in assessment phase (solvent test). Adhesion primer mandatory when oil-based existing coating identified. ASTM D3359 adhesion test at representative locations.

risk_notes.risk: Using latex primer instead of shellac stain blocker on contaminated trim. PVA and acrylic primers have ZERO stain blocking capability (RC-002). Profile crevices trap concentrated smoke deposits.
risk_notes.mitigation: Proper contamination identification during assessment. Shellac-based stain blocker (BIN) for smoke damage — full surface, ensure crevice coverage.

risk_notes.topic: Scrape edges telegraphing through trim finish
risk_notes.risk: Failure to feather-sand scrape edges before priming. Old paint edge creates a visible ridge especially conspicuous on trim at close viewing distance.
risk_notes.mitigation: Feather-sand all scrape edges to create smooth transition. Non-negotiable at all tiers. 120-150 grit for initial feathering.

risk_notes.topic: Short working time with urethane-modified products
risk_notes.risk: Overworking Advance or Emerald Urethane causes roping, brush marks, or orange peel on trim finish.
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Sand marks out between coats with rigid block. Build finish through multiple sanded coats.

risk_notes.topic: Wall surface damage during trim painting
risk_notes.risk: Inadequate wall masking allowing paint transfer from trim work to finished wall surface in occupied home.
risk_notes.mitigation: Proper wall masking: tape at wall-trim junction for brush; tape + paper masking for spray. Remove tape while finish is slightly tacky for cleanest pull.

risk_notes.risk: Shellac stain blocker (BIN) has strong alcohol odor — occupant discomfort in occupied residential spaces.
risk_notes.mitigation: Ensure adequate ventilation (open windows, fans). Use PPE (respirator). Coordinate with homeowner on timing — fast dry (~45 min) but strong odor during application. Consider temporary occupant relocation from affected rooms.

risk_notes.topic: Gloss finish magnifies imperfections at QT5
risk_notes.risk: Every brush mark, dust nib, and sanding scratch shows in gloss finish on trim.
risk_notes.mitigation: 3 coats with thorough 220-320 grit sanding between each. Meticulous dust cleanup (tack cloth). Controlled environment. Rigid sanding block mandatory.

material_notes.selection_guidance: This spec uses TWO material selection drivers: (1) Primer selection is SUBSTRATE STATE driven — SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT for sound/failing/peeling paint, SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT for smoke damage, SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT for moisture damage. (2) Finish selection is QUALITY TIER driven — SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC at QT3, SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE at QT4, SYS_FF_PREMIUM at QT5. These are independent axes.
material_notes.primer_vs_nc: NC trim primer selection is SUBSTRATE MATERIAL driven (bare wood type). RP primer selection is COATING CONDITION driven (existing paint state). NC primer systems (SYS_TRIM_HIGHBUILD, SYS_MDF_EDGE_SEAL, SYS_MDF_FACE_PRIME, SYS_STAIN_BLOCK, SYS_STANDARD_PRIME, SYS_BONDING_PRIME) are NOT used in this RP spec — replaced by shared RP primer systems.
material_notes.finish_identical_to_nc: Finish material systems (SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, SYS_FF_PREMIUM) are identical to NC trim finish because once the surface is properly prepped and primed, the finish application is the same. SYS_FF_GALLERY omitted from RP — gallery-series systems are new construction specification only.
material_notes.coverage_is_lf_based: All coverage profiles are LF-based per PDCA standard (1 LF trim = 1 SF). Profile complexity affects effective coverage: simple profiles have less surface area per LF (higher coverage), ornate profiles have more surface area (lower coverage). Coverage profiles are split by profile complexity rather than using a single rate with a modifier.
material_notes.caulk_rate_difference: RP caulk yield is ~250 LF/tube vs NC 72 LF/tube because RP is selective replacement (15-30% of joints) rather than full application. This is a significant materials cost difference.
material_notes.consumable_differences_from_nc: RP adds: CON_ASSESSMENT_KIT (adhesion/coating ID), CON_DEGLOSS_LIQUID (chemical degloss), CON_SCRAPER_CONTOUR (profile scraping), CON_SANDING_SPONGE_CONTOUR (profile sanding), CON_DENATURED_ALCOHOL (shellac cleanup). RP removes: CON_FILLER_WOOD (end grain fill), CON_SANDPAPER_SHEET_120 for MDF edge sanding, CON_DENATURED_ALCOHOL for MDF/FJP shellac (replaced by same item for smoke damage shellac).

assumptions.value: 350-500 LF/gal depending on primer type and profile complexity
assumptions.source: Adapted from NC trim prime coverage rates with adjustment for previously painted substrate (lower absorption = higher coverage)
assumptions.note: Adhesion primer on painted trim has higher coverage than bare-wood primer due to lower porosity. Stain blocker has lower coverage due to higher solids.
Finish coverage is identical to NC because primed surface condition is equivalent after proper RP prep and prime.

assumptions.value: 15-30% of joints need replacement in typical RP
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines post-original-caulk failure rate. Estimated from field experience. Marked for field validation.
No doctrine coverage for degloss liquid quantity. Based on manufacturer spec. Application method (wipe-on with rag) affects actual usage.
